prs.title: fix: keep what a step installs for the next one, and give jobs the runner's Rust and Docker
prs.body:
## Why

After #171, three of the eight repositories in the sweep still failed locally on runs that pass on GitHub, for two reasons:

| Cause | Repos hit |
|---|---|
| Nothing outside the workspace survived between steps, because each step was a new container | cobra (`go install`), ky's browser job (`playwright install --with-deps`), rust-lang/log (`rustup toolchain add`) |
| The runner image had no `rustup` or `docker` | rust-lang/log, cobra's licence job |

## What changes

**One container per job is the default.** It existed behind `--job-container`. It is now how a job's `run:` steps run on Docker and Podman.
- `--step-containers` or `WRKFLW_STEP_CONTAINERS=1` gives each step its own container again; `--preserve-containers-on-failure` still implies that.
- `--job-container` is still accepted and does nothing.
- The jobs of a called workflow share a container too, so their services now start.

**The job container's memory is measured.** It wasn't sampled before, so such a job was treated as never measured and a matrix ran one leg at a time on a small VM. The job's container and its services are now sampled through the CLI's `stats`, with the same out-of-memory and cancelled-step handling a step's own container has. Podman jobs stay unmeasured, as before.

**Jobs that use the runner's Rust get it.** A job whose `run:` steps call `cargo`, `rustup`, `rustc` or `rustfmt` without a Rust setup action gets rustup and `stable` in its image, as hosted runners have. An image mapped with `-P`, or a `rust` image, keeps its own, and a base that has rustup keeps its default toolchain.

**Which steps run `docker` or `cargo` is read as a shell splits the script:** multi-line quotes and heredocs stay whole, `bash -c '...'` and a heredoc a shell reads are looked into, and `command -v docker` doesn't count.

**Stored results are keyed on the container mode** (key version 4), so a pass with a container per step isn't reused under the new default.

**`--docker-in-jobs` (opt-in).** With it, or `WRKFLW_DOCKER_IN_JOBS=1`, a job whose steps run `docker` gets a Docker engine of its own inside its container.
- That container runs privileged, which is why it is off by default.
- The machine's engine is never handed to a step: `-v $(pwd):/wrk` would then name a path on the machine, not in the job, and a check could pass on an empty directory.
- Without the flag, the run warns once that those steps will fail and names the flag.
- Docker only: on Podman the run says those steps will fail.

## Breaking

- A workflow that only passed locally because each step started from a clean image now behaves as on GitHub.
- A job that calls `cargo` with no setup action builds an image on its first run.
- Library: `Acceleration::job_container` is replaced by `step_containers` (its opposite), and `docker_in_jobs` is new.
- `--reuse-results` reruns every job once, as the result key's version changed.

All of this is in `BREAKING_CHANGES.md`.

## Testing

- `cargo test --workspace`: all pass, including three Docker-backed tests in `container_fidelity_test` (one new: what a step installs is there for the next, and isn't with `--step-containers`).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- Real runs on Docker Desktop (7.7 GB VM), with workflows written for this:
  - a step finds the `apt-get` package and the `$HOME/bin` tool the previous step installed; with `--step-containers` it fails as before
  - `rustup toolchain add beta` and `rustup target add` are there for the `cargo` step after them
  - `docker run -v $(pwd):/wrk` reads the workspace with `--docker-in-jobs`, and no container or volume is left behind
  - a three-leg matrix is measured on its first run

## Benchmark

pallets/click at 1077444 against GitHub run 42384079679, release build, Docker Desktop (7.7 GB VM), images already built:

| Mode | Runs (s) | Agree |
|---|---|---|
| One container per job (new default) | 121 (first, result key changed), 71, 72, 55 | 11/11 every run |
| `WRKFLW_STEP_CONTAINERS=1` | 67, 62 | 11/11 |

Both modes take about the same time, so the new default doesn't slow click down. Both are slower than the 36–38 s measured on 2026-11-12, and `--step-containers` is just as slow, so the default isn't the cause. The cause isn't known yet.

## Review fixes (87e9199)

- The runner's Rust and the setup action's Rust use one rustup script. It downloads the installer to a file and checks `rustup --version` before linking, so a failed download fails the image build. Before this, the piped installer exited 0 with no rustup, and that Rust-less image was kept and reused. Checked in containers: offline it now fails (exit 127 without curl, 6 with it); online it installs cargo 1.100; an image with rustup is left as it is.
- An image mapped with `-P` gets no Docker engine, just as it gets no Rust. Under `--docker-in-jobs` the run says that image must bring its own engine.
- A `case` pattern is no longer read as a command, and `<<` inside `$((...))` is no longer read as a heredoc.
- Memory samples can no longer land after the session has taken its containers off the meter.

## Not verified

- The eight-repo sweep has not been rerun with this branch, so the agreement count on those repos is still unknown.
- Podman was not run; `--docker-in-jobs` is now refused there rather than tried.
- Real runs after the review fixes (Docker Desktop): a `-P` image gets no Rust layer (`cargo: command not found`, as in the image), the default image has it; `command -v docker` raises no warning; `bash -c 'docker run -v $(pwd):/wrk ...'` warns without the flag and passes with it, leaving no container; a shared-container pass is not reused under `--step-containers`.
